## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r nearest neighbor}
#Subset the integrated data by sample name

sample1 <- subset(data, subset = sample == "sample1")
sample2 <- subset(data, subset = sample == "sample2")
sample3 <- subset(data, subset = sample == "sample3")
sample4 <- subset(data, subset = sample == "sample4")
sample5 <- subset(data, subset = sample == "sample5")
sample6 <- subset(data, subset = sample == "sample6")
sample7 <- subset(data, subset = sample == "sample7")

# Step 1 — extract coordinates for each
coords_subset1 <- GetTissueCoordinates(sample1)
coords_subset2 <- GetTissueCoordinates(sample2)
coords_subset3 <- GetTissueCoordinates(sample3)
coords_subset4 <- GetTissueCoordinates(sample4)
coords_subset5 <- GetTissueCoordinates(sample5)
coords_subset6 <- GetTissueCoordinates(sample6)
coords_subset7 <- GetTissueCoordinates(sample7)

# Ensure rownames are set to the cell ID for Sample 1
rownames(coords_subset1) <- coords_subset1$cell

# Identify cell_type1 cells and cell_type2 cells based on sample1$celltype
cell_type1_spots   <- rownames(coords_subset1)[sample1$celltype[coords_subset1$cell] == "cell_type1"]
cell_type2_spots <- rownames(coords_subset1)[sample1$celltype[coords_subset1$cell] == "cell_type2"]

# Subset the coordinates
coords_cell_type1 <- coords_subset1[cell_type1_spots, c("x","y"), drop = FALSE]
coords_cell_type2   <- coords_subset1[cell_type2_spots, c("x","y"), drop = FALSE]

nn <- get.knnx(
  data  = as.matrix(coords_cell_type2),    # reference points (Cell Type 2)
  query = as.matrix(coords_cell_type1),  # query points (Cell type 1)
  k     = 1
)


# Distances from cell type1 to nearest cell type2
distances_cell1 <- nn$nn.dist

summary(distances_cell1)

# repeat for each sample
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
